trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 22:30. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or the RENFE train (€4.60) to the city center. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Take a short stroll along the nearby Barceloneta beachfront promenade to decompress after the flight — it's lively at night in summer.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour convenience store or a local kebab/bocadillo shop near the hotel (budget: €5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — just settle in. Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card the next morning (€11.35) to save on transport throughout the trip. August in Barcelona is hot and humid; stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a free walk along Barceloneta Beach right from the hotel — enjoy the morning sea breeze before the heat peaks. Then head to the iconic Palau de la Música Catalana or walk up La Rambla toward the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic). Explore the narrow medieval streets, the Plaça Reial, and the Barcelona Cathedral exterior (free to enter the cloister). This entire area is walkable and historically rich.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Picasso Museum (€12 general admission; free on Thursday evenings). Afterward, explore El Born neighborhood — browse local boutiques and street art. Walk to Parc de la Ciutadella (free entry) for a relaxing afternoon break under the shade; see the monumental fountain and rent a rowboat on the lake (€6 for 45 min, optional).
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Barceloneta for the famous Barcelona nightlife warm-up. Visit the Chiringuito (beach bars) along the boardwalk for a cheap beer or sangria (€3–5). Later, explore the free outdoor terraces around Passeig del Born — a hub for locals starting their night out.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh croissant and café con leche at a local bakery near the hotel (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Bocadillo and fresh juice at Mercat de Santa Caterina — a less-touristy alternative to La Boqueria with cheaper prices (€6–8)
meals.dinner: Set menu (Menú del Día) at a local restaurant in El Born or Gothic Quarter — typically includes starter, main, dessert, and drink for €10–13

day_by_day.notes: Avoid La Boqueria for meals — it's touristy and overpriced. Santa Caterina Market is a great budget-friendly alternative. Wear comfortable walking shoes; you'll cover 8–10 km today.

day_by_day.morning: Today is dedicated to Gaudí architecture. Start early (before 9:00 AM) at the Sagrada Família — book tickets online in advance to avoid queues (€26 with tower access, or €20 basic entry). The morning light through the stained glass is spectacular. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring this UNESCO World Heritage masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro to Diagonal and visit Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) from the outside — the facades are free to admire and photograph. Walk through the Eixample neighborhood to appreciate the grid layout and Modernista architecture. Then head to Park Güell — the monumental zone requires a ticket (€10, book online), but the surrounding park and terraces are free and offer stunning city views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Gràcia neighborhood near Park Güell — a bohemian, local district full of affordable tapas bars and terraces. Join the evening paseo culture. Later, if you're up for nightlife, head to Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz (both in Poblenou, near the hotel area) — Barcelona's legendary clubs with entry around €12–15 including a drink.

meals.breakfast: Toast with tomato (Pa amb Tomàquet) and coffee at a café in Eixample (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Grab a bocadillo or empanada from a local bakery near Sagrada Família (€4–6) — eat in a nearby park to save money
meals.dinner: Tapas crawl in Gràcia neighborhood — order patatas bravas, croquetas, and pan con tomate at local bars (€2–4 per tapa; budget €12–15 total)

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance for August — they sell out fast. Park Güell timed slots also sell out; book online to save €2 vs. on-site. Wear sunscreen; August sun is intense.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Espanya station and visit Montjuïc hill. Ride the free escalators up or take the cable car (€11.50 return, optional). Explore the free exterior of the Palau Nacional (MNAC) with its sweeping city views. Visit the Olympic Stadium (Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys) — entry is free. Enjoy the panoramic views over Barcelona from the hilltop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Poble Sec neighborhood — one of Barcelona's most authentic and affordable barrios. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (€14 entry) for world-class modern art. Alternatively, if budget is tight, explore the free street murals and architecture of Poble Sec. Head to Avinguda del Paral·lel for a stroll and local café stop.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Barceloneta beachfront area near the hotel. Enjoy a sunset swim at the beach (free). Then explore the W Barcelona hotel area and Port Olímpic — the marina is lively with free outdoor entertainment in summer. For nightlife, Port Olímpic has numerous clubs and beach bars; cover charges vary (€5–15) but many offer free entry before midnight.

meals.breakfast: Fresh orange juice and a pastry from a local market or café near the hotel (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Montjuïc — buy supplies at a Mercadona or Lidl supermarket (baguette, cheese, fruit, water for €5–7)
meals.dinner: Authentic paella or fideuà at a local restaurant in Barceloneta — look for set menus or lunch specials offered in the evening (€12–16); avoid the overpriced seafront tourist traps

day_by_day.notes: The Montjuïc Magic Fountain show runs on weekend evenings in summer (free!) — check the schedule as it may fall on a Friday or weekend. Poble Sec has some of Barcelona's best value pintxos bars on Carrer de Blai — a must-visit street.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise walk or swim at Barceloneta Beach — the sea is calm and crowds are minimal at dawn. Pack up and check out of the hotel. Drop luggage at the hotel reception if your flight is later in the day. Take one last stroll along the Port Vell (Old Port) — walk across the Rambla del Mar wooden bridge and admire the sailboats. Visit the Columbus Monument (exterior free; lift to top €6, optional).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, spend final hours browsing the El Raval neighborhood for last-minute affordable souvenirs (avoid La Rambla tourist shops — prices are inflated). Visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) exterior plaza — a popular skate spot and social hub — free to enjoy the vibe. Head to the airport via Aerobus or RENFE train with plenty of time to spare.

meals.breakfast: Final café con leche and croissant at a local bar near the hotel (€2–3) — sit at the bar for cheaper prices vs. table service
meals.lunch: Grab a bocadillo or slice of pizza from a takeaway near Port Vell or El Raval (€4–6) — eat on a bench by the waterfront

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure to reach Barcelona El Prat Airport from the city center in August (summer traffic and airport queues can be long). Keep €10–15 cash for transport to the airport. A T-Casual metro card should cover all your transport needs throughout the trip if purchased on Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — no morning activities scheduled. Flight UA lands at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival day — no afternoon activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for landing.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort on the Beachfront (~30–40 min by taxi or Aerobus + cab). Check in, freshen up, and take a short relaxing stroll along the beachfront promenade to decompress from travel. Grab a light late-night snack near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour beach bar or hotel bar — try a bocadillo (Spanish sandwich) and a cold Estrella Damm beer. Budget ~€10–15.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid long taxi queues late at night. Store luggage efficiently and get to bed early to start Day 2 refreshed. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements for late arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a leisurely breakfast at the hotel or a nearby beachfront café. Then head to the Sagrada Família Guided Tour (book the first morning slot, ~9:00–10:30 AM). Explore Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica with a skip-the-line guided tour, marveling at the intricate facades, towering spires, and stunning stained-glass interior. (~2 hours including travel)
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take the metro to the Eixample district for lunch. Then embark on the Gaudí Architecture Walking Tour (~2:00–5:00 PM), covering Casa Batlló, Casa Milà (La Pedrera), and Palau Güell. Discover the history and symbolism behind Gaudí's masterpieces with an expert guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up. Head to the Gothic Quarter for dinner at a mid-range tapas restaurant. Afterward, join the Gothic Quarter Night Bar Crawl (~9:30 PM start), visiting hidden cocktail bars and atmospheric venues through the medieval labyrinthine streets.

meals.breakfast: Café with pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) and coffee at a local bakery near the hotel. Budget ~€6–10.
meals.lunch: Lunch near the Eixample — try a menú del día (set lunch menu) at a local restaurant: starter, main, dessert, and drink for ~€13–16.
meals.dinner: Tapas dinner in the Gothic Quarter — patatas bravas, croquetas, jamón, and pan con tomate at a mid-range tapas bar. Budget ~€20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Sagrada Família tickets online well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead in August. The Gaudí Walking Tour often includes Casa Batlló entry; confirm what's included when booking. Wear comfortable walking shoes — today involves significant walking.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning at the beach directly accessible from the Aegean Bliss Resort. Swim, sunbathe, and recharge on Barceloneta Beach. Grab a coffee and breakfast at one of the beachfront chiringuitos (beach bars). This is your balanced rest morning after a busy Day 2.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, visit the Palau de la Música Catalana for a self-guided or short guided daytime tour of the exterior and interior (~2:00–3:30 PM) to appreciate the stunning Art Nouveau architecture before the evening concert. Then explore the El Born neighborhood nearby — browse boutique shops, street art, and the Mercat de Santa Caterina.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert (~8:00 or 9:00 PM). Experience a live performance inside the breathtaking UNESCO-listed concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The ornate stained-glass skylight and mosaic columns make this a magical architectural and cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Beachfront chiringuito breakfast — fresh orange juice, croissant, and café con leche. Budget ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch on Barceloneta — try a paella or fideuà at a mid-range restaurant. Budget ~€18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner in El Born — a stylish mid-range restaurant with Catalan cuisine. Try escalivada or suquet de peix. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Palau de la Música Catalana concert tickets in advance at palaumusica.cat — August programs often feature flamenco, classical, or jazz. Smart casual dress is recommended for the concert. The daytime architectural visit is separate from the concert ticket.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or a scenic walk up to Park Güell (open from ~8:00 AM — arrive early to beat the crowds and August heat). Explore Gaudí's whimsical park with its mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and panoramic views over Barcelona. (~2 hours)
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Park Güell and head to the Gràcia neighborhood for lunch. Spend the afternoon exploring the charming Gràcia district — its bohemian plazas, independent shops, and street art. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies or simply wander the Passeig de Gràcia for window shopping and architecture spotting. Return to the hotel late afternoon for a swim and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Tonight is your big nightlife night — head to Clubbing at Razzmatazz, one of Europe's most iconic nightclubs in a converted warehouse with five rooms, each playing a different music genre. Doors typically open ~1:00 AM; pre-game with dinner and drinks in the El Poblenou neighborhood nearby.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before Park Güell — grab a pastry and coffee from a local bakery near the hotel or metro stop. Budget ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Gràcia — try a mid-range Catalan bistro or a trendy brunch spot. Budget ~€14–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in El Poblenou near Razzmatazz — a hip industrial-chic restaurant or craft beer bar with food. Budget ~€20–28 per person. Eat late (9:00–10:30 PM) in true Barcelona style before the club.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell's monumental zone requires timed entry tickets — book online in advance at parkguell.barcelona. For Razzmatazz, check their website for the specific Wednesday night program and buy tickets online to avoid queues. Expect to stay out until 3:00–5:00 AM — plan Day 5 accordingly with a late start.

day_by_day.morning: Late, relaxed start after the Razzmatazz night — sleep in and enjoy a slow brunch. Head to the Barceloneta neighborhood for a final leisurely beach morning. Take one last swim in the Mediterranean and soak up the Barcelona sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: After checking out or leaving luggage with the hotel, explore the Montjuïc area — take the cable car or funicular up for panoramic city views. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (mid-range entry ~€14) for a dose of Barcelona's art scene, or simply enjoy the gardens and fortress views. Head back down via the Paral·lel neighborhood for last-minute souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Barcelona at a rooftop restaurant in the Eixample or a classic Catalan restaurant in the Gothic Quarter. Raise a glass of cava to an incredible trip before heading to the airport or retiring for the night.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at a beachfront café — eggs, fresh juice, and coffee. Budget ~€12–18.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Montjuïc — a café or museum restaurant. Budget ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range rooftop or Catalan restaurant — try a tasting menu or à la carte with local wine. Budget ~€30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If departing by air on Day 5 or Day 6, confirm hotel late checkout or luggage storage options with Aegean Bliss Resort. Montjuïc cable car may have queues in August — go mid-afternoon to avoid peak times. Book the farewell dinner reservation in advance for the best rooftop spots.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from Barcelona–El Prat Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort, Beachfront. Check-in, unwind with a welcome amenity, and enjoy the resort's sea-view suite.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival only. After check-in, enjoy a light welcome drink at the resort's rooftop bar overlooking the Mediterranean. Room service or in-hotel dining available for a late-night bite.

meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — request a curated charcuterie board, local Catalan cheeses, and a bottle of Cava to celebrate arrival in Barcelona.

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-arranged. Confirm early check-in or luggage storage if needed. Keep the first evening low-key to recover from travel and prepare for a full Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Then embark on the Sagrada Família Guided Tour — skip-the-line access ensures a seamless, premium experience. Spend 2–3 hours marveling at Gaudí's unfinished basilica, including tower access for panoramic views of Barcelona. A private guide is recommended for an in-depth architectural narrative.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Eixample district for the Gaudí Architecture Walking Tour, covering Casa Batlló, Casa Milà (La Pedrera), and Palau Güell. Opt for a private guide to explore the Modernisme movement at a relaxed luxury pace. Includes rooftop access at La Pedrera with stunning city views. Stop for a mid-afternoon coffee at a designer café in the Eixample.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert — a breathtaking UNESCO-listed venue designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Dress to impress for this world-class cultural experience. After the concert, enjoy a late dinner in El Born neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Grand buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort's beachfront restaurant — fresh pastries, Iberian cold cuts, seasonal fruit, and made-to-order eggs.
meals.lunch: Disfrutar Restaurant (2 Michelin stars) — avant-garde Catalan cuisine in a stunning Mediterranean-inspired setting. Reserve well in advance.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — a beloved Catalan wine bar and tapas spot post-concert, followed by a nightcap at Bar Marsella, one of Barcelona's oldest cocktail bars.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família skip-the-line tickets and Palau de la Música concert tickets in advance. Private guides for the architecture tour can be arranged through the hotel concierge. Dress code applies for the evening concert — smart casual to semi-formal.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a slow, indulgent morning at the resort. Take advantage of the beachfront location — a private beach cabana, morning swim in the Mediterranean, or a spa treatment at the resort's luxury wellness center. Optional: sunrise yoga session on the beach if offered by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) on a self-guided or private walking tour. Wander through narrow medieval lanes, visit the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden courtyards. Stop into high-end boutiques and local artisan galleries. Visit the Picasso Museum for a cultural afternoon interlude (book tickets in advance).
day_by_day.evening: Gothic Quarter Night Bar Crawl — join an organized premium bar crawl through the atmospheric Gothic Quarter, visiting hidden cocktail bars and speakeasies. This curated experience pairs perfectly with the neighborhood's medieval architecture and vibrant nightlife energy.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at the resort's terrace restaurant — freshly squeezed juices, smoked salmon, avocado toast, and artisan pastries with sea views.
meals.lunch: Senyor Parellada in the Gothic Quarter — elegant Catalan cuisine in a beautifully restored 18th-century building. Try the esqueixada de bacallà and crema catalana.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda — a sophisticated wine-focused restaurant with an exceptional Catalan menu. Pre-crawl dinner to fuel the evening ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for Gothic Quarter exploration — cobblestones can be challenging. The night bar crawl typically starts around 21:00–22:00; confirm meeting point with the organizer. Keep valuables secure in the Gothic Quarter at night.

day_by_day.morning: Private yacht or luxury catamaran morning excursion along the Barcelona coastline — arrange through the hotel concierge. Enjoy champagne, fresh fruit, and stunning views of the city skyline from the sea. Optional snorkeling or paddleboarding. Return to the resort by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Montjuïc Hill — take the cable car for panoramic views of Barcelona and the Mediterranean. Explore the Fundació Joan Miró (world-class modern art collection), the Montjuïc Castle, and the beautifully landscaped gardens. Enjoy a leisurely stroll and photography session with sweeping city views.
day_by_day.evening: Clubbing at Razzmatazz — one of Europe's most iconic nightclubs, housed in a converted warehouse with five distinct rooms, each featuring different music genres. Arrive after midnight for peak atmosphere. VIP table or bottle service recommended for a premium experience.

meals.breakfast: Light continental breakfast at the resort or on the yacht — croissants, tropical fruits, yogurt, and freshly brewed coffee.
meals.lunch: Quimet & Quimet (El Poble Sec) — legendary standing bar famous for creative montaditos and premium tinned seafood. A beloved Barcelona institution near Montjuïc.
meals.dinner: Tickets Restaurant by Albert Adrià (advance reservation essential) — avant-garde tapas in a theatrical setting. One of Barcelona's most exciting and coveted dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Yacht excursion must be booked at least 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge. Razzmatazz opens late — plan dinner no earlier than 21:00 to align with Barcelona's nightlife rhythm. VIP entry or table reservations at Razzmatazz should be arranged in advance to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast on the beachfront terrace. Take a final swim in the Mediterranean or a relaxing spa session. Arrange late checkout if possible (confirm with the hotel). Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last exploration of Barcelona — visit the upscale Passeig de Gràcia boulevard for luxury shopping (Loewe, Hermès, Balenciaga flagship stores). Browse the Mercat de Santa Caterina for gourmet local products and souvenirs. Enjoy a final coffee and people-watching at a chic café terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a rooftop restaurant with panoramic Barcelona views before heading to the airport or continuing the journey. Arrange private luxury transfer for departure.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full spread including Iberian ham, artisan cheeses, fresh pastries, eggs Benedict, and premium Cava mimosas.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Passeig de Gràcia — beloved local spot for premium tapas, fresh seafood, and cold craft beers. Perfect for a relaxed final lunch.
meals.dinner: Azimut Rooftop Restaurant or similar panoramic venue — contemporary Mediterranean cuisine with sweeping views of Barcelona at golden hour. Toast to an unforgettable trip with a glass of local Priorat wine.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm late checkout with the hotel in advance to maximize the final day without luggage stress. Pre-book private airport transfer for a seamless, stress-free departure. Purchase any last-minute gifts or gourmet items (olive oil, Cava, artisan chocolates) at Mercat de Santa Caterina or El Corte Inglés Gourmet Experience on Plaça de Catalunya.
